title: MLCC Deployment-Target Descriptor
description: Per-deployment-target descriptor. The single source of truth for a target's contract (status var, success status, config schema, verb applicability). The scattered authorities (do/config template, _guard_deployment_active, do-config.js SHELL_VAR_TO_ANSWER, regenerate RUNTIME_OWNED_VARS, the deploy/clean dispatchers, deploy_schema.py) DERIVE from these descriptors instead of hardcoding per-target knowledge. See ADR-008.

target.description: Canonical target key; matches the descriptor directory name (e.g. realtime-inference, eks).

aliases.description: Backward-compatible alias names that normalize to `target` (e.g. managed-inference -> realtime-inference). Empty [] when none.

status_var.description: The per-target state variable written to do/config on deploy success/failure. Read by _guard_deployment_active.

answer_key.description: The camelCase generator-answer key for status_var, used by do-config.js SHELL_VAR_TO_ANSWER.

success_status.description: The status_var value that means 'active' for this target. Must be one of the states _guard_deployment_active accepts.

family.description: Deployment family. sagemaker-endpoint: real-time/async managed endpoints. sagemaker-job: batch transform. kubernetes: served as k8s pods (hyperpod-eks via the operator, eks without it).

deploy_script.description: Path (relative to do/) of the deploy dispatcher target script.

clean_script.description: Path (relative to do/) of the teardown target script.

required_vars.description: Config vars that must be non-empty before deploy (deploy_schema.py SCHEMAS.required).

optional_vars.description: Optional config vars with their default values (deploy_schema.py SCHEMAS.optional).

runtime_owned_vars.description: Vars this target writes at runtime that `mcc regenerate` must PRESERVE (feed regenerate's RUNTIME_OWNED_VARS). Always includes status_var; add any other per-target runtime-written vars. Cross-target/global runtime vars (VLLM_*, HP_SPECULATIVE_*, benchmark, mlflow) stay in the shared set, not here.

serving_config_source.description: Which resolve-serving-config.sh resolution arm this target uses. kubernetes: reads HP_*/BENCHMARK_* (hyperpod-eks, eks). sagemaker-ic: reads DEPLOYED_INSTANCE_TYPE/IC_ENV_* (realtime, async, batch).

verbs.description: Per-verb applicability for verbs that are target-restricted. true = the verb applies to this target; false = the verb refuses it (exit 3). Only verbs that vary by target need listing (optimize, add-ic, ci, adapter, draft). Verbs with `targets: all` are not listed.

answer_params.description: The single source of truth for this target's deploy answer-key plumbing (see docs/adr/ADR-008 and .kiro/steering/derive-dont-hardcode.md). Each entry ties an answer key (DEPLOY_ANSWERS JSON key) to its config var, optional CLI flag, and roles. The four historical tables — CLI_FLAG_TO_VARS (deploy-config-builder.js), flag_to_answer_key (.deploy_helper.py), _ANSWER_KEY_TO_VAR (deploy_prompts.py), and the inline KEY_MAP (do/deploy) — plus do/deploy's flag arg-parse arms and both forwarding blocks all DERIVE from the union of these per-target arrays. Option B: every target lists all its params independently (including core target/instance_type) so a target can add or target-scope a param without touching a shared table; a conformance test enforces that any answerKey shared across targets maps to the same configVar.

configVar.description: The SCREAMING_SNAKE config/env var the answer key resolves to.

flag.description: The CLI flag (do/deploy) that supplies this value. Present only for roles that include flag-input.

roles.description: flag-input: has a CLI flag; appears in builder/helper flag tables, do/deploy arg-parse arms, and both forwarding blocks. prompt-core: the core target/instance_type params handled specially by the builder but still answer keys on the Python side. internal: no flag; produced by prompts/builder; part of the DEPLOY_ANSWERS input surface (_ANSWER_KEY_TO_VAR). builder-output: emitted only in the Node builder's JSON output (do/deploy KEY_MAP); no flag, no prompt input. input-only: a flag/prompt/internal param the builder does NOT re-emit, so it is excluded from the output KEY_MAP (e.g. endpoint_name, re-emitted target-scoped as smai_/async_endpoint_name; hp_instance_group_name).
